steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION foo() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO audit VALUES(TG_OP); RETURN NULL; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql
CREATE TRIGGER table_trigger AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON foo_table FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION foo()
SELECT event FROM audit ORDER BY event

cases.adaptation: This trigger fixture observes durable audit rows; notification callbacks have separate notify fixtures. These SQL steps execute sequentially and do not claim script atomicity.

steps.sql: CREATE FUNCTION foo() RETURNS event_trigger AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO audit VALUES(TG_TAG); END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql
CREATE EVENT TRIGGER pglite_event ON ddl_command_end EXECUTE FUNCTION foo()
SELECT tag FROM audit ORDER BY tag

cases.adaptation: Observe SQL audit rows rather than a PGlite notification callback; SQL-drop negative assertion retained.
cleanup: DROP EVENT TRIGGER IF EXISTS pglite_event
